message.content:
**Boiling eggs—step‑by‑step guide** | Goal | Time & Tips | |------|-------------| | **Soft‑boiled** (runny yolk) | 4–5 min after water boils
• Use room‑temperature eggs so shells don’t crack.
• Drop them gently into simmering water using a slotted spoon.
• Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop further cooking. | | **Medium** (slightly runny center) | 7–8 min after water boils
• Same drop technique as above. | | **Hard‑boiled** (fully set yolks) | 10–12 min after water boils
• For larger eggs, add ~1 minute per inch beyond 2½″ diameter. | ### General Steps 1. **Prep the Eggs** - Let eggs sit at room temp (~15 min out of fridge). - Gently tap each egg against a counter to loosen shell cracks before placing it in hot water. 2. **Heat Water** - Fill a saucepan with enough cold water to cover eggs by ~1 inch. - Bring to a rolling boil over high heat. 3. **Add Eggs Carefully** - Reduce flame slightly to avoid splashing. - Lower eggs one at a time with a slotted spoon into the pot. 4. **Start Timing Once Boil Restarts** - As soon as the water returns to a gentle boil, start your timer according to desired doneness. 5. **Cool Quickly After Cooking** - Remove eggs from hot water immediately when time’s up. - Place them straight into an ice‑water bath (or running cool water) for 5–10 minutes to halt cooking and make peeling easier. 6. **Peel or Store** - Crack all around then peel under running water. - If storing, keep peeled eggs refrigerated and consume within a week. --- #### Quick “One‑Size” Rule of Thumb If you’re unsure which doneness level you prefer, aim for **9 minutes** – this gives a firm white but still creamy yolk, suitable for most uses like salads or sandwiches. Feel free to tweak the time by ±30 seconds depending on altitude, stove power, or personal preference!
